newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain cuts Spanish interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain cuts Spanish interest rates.

text.p: The Bank of Spain said on Friday it had cut its key money rate to 5.75 percent from 6.00 percent.
The rate, which followed a regular repurchase tender for central bank certificates, was followed by similar cuts by a series of commercial banks.
The Bank of Spain last cut its rates on January 16 having started the move to lower rates in December 1995 when the key money market rate was reduced to 9.00 percent from 9.25 percent.
"I was surprised because it seems to me it is based only on good February CPI, shrugging off other things such as the peseta's weakness," economist Gregorio Gomez said.
"We'll see the reaction in the market in the following days..it could be the last time they cut"
Carmen Hernansanz, economist at Merrill Lynch Espana said, however, the Bank of Spain had responded with its usual caution.
"I think the Bank of Spain has earned its reputation with caution so, if it cuts rates, it's because it is reasonably satisfied with prices and this generates confidence in the markets."
